title: Two formulations of bounded-error decision
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let $L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ be a language, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. The machine halts within time $T$ and outputs the indicator of $L$ with probability at least $2/3$ on every input if and only if it halts within time $T$ and outputs that indicator with probability at least the constant function $2/3$ on every input.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$T$ maps input lengths to natural-number time bounds
